# A 5 kWh battery carries *80% of summer evenings*; doubling it adds 9 points for 3,700 € more.

What size of battery to add to a 6 kW rooftop array on a four-person house, from an installer's quote and a year of meter readings.

**Decide:** pick one of the three sizes in the question below, a minute.

<h2 data-nav="System">The battery sits behind the inverter</h2>

<Explore controls={[{ id: "hour", label: "Time of day", choice: { morning: "Morning", evening: "Evening", night: "Night" } }]} frame={supplier} />

<div class="beside" data-width="full">

- <span data-ref="panels">1</span> The <span data-ref="panels">panels</span> stay as they are.
- <span data-ref="inverter">2</span> The <span data-ref="inverter">hybrid inverter</span> replaces the string inverter and decides where each kWh goes.
- <span data-ref="battery">3</span> The <span data-ref="battery">battery</span> takes the surplus and gives it back in the evening.
- <span data-ref="grid">4</span> The <span data-ref="grid">grid</span> covers what is left, through a new bidirectional meter.


```mermaid tag:panels=1 tag:inverter=2 tag:battery=3 tag:grid=4

	inverter --> house["House"]

	battery -->|"evening"| inverter
	grid["Grid"] -->|"shortfall"| house
```

</div>

The status lamp on the inverter is wired like this:

```schematic
title Status lamp: a 12 V supply, a series resistor and an LED
VB battery vcc 0 12 V @0,0 v
R_lim resistor vcc lamp 680 a@VB.a 6,0 v
D1 led lamp 0 green b@R_lim.b 0,4 v
```

The <span data-ref="R_lim">series resistor</span> sets the lamp's current, about 16 mA.

# How the numbers were made

<div class="beside">
<div>

A year of hourly meter readings, scaled to the quote's battery sizes with a simple charge model: each hour the <span data-ref="surplus">surplus</span> charges the battery up to its size, losing a tenth on the way (its <Term recall="round-trip">round trip</Term>), and a shortfall draws it down before the grid is asked.

</div>

```ts ref:surplus="surplus"
for (const hour of year) {
	const surplus = hour.produced - hour.used;
	stored = surplus > 0
		? Math.min(size, stored + surplus * 0.9)
		: Math.max(0, stored + surplus);
}
```

</div>

## Assumptions

| Input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Array | 6 kW, south, 35° |
| Use | 4,920 kWh a year |
| Bought | 0.22 €/kWh |
| Sold | 0.06 €/kWh |
| Battery round trip | 90% |

## Not included

Price changes, battery wear after year ten, and any subsidy, which would shorten the <Term recall="payback">payback</Term>.

<Recall id="round-trip">A battery's **round trip** is the share of the energy put in that comes back out, here 90%.</Recall>

<Recall id="payback">The **payback** time is the price over the yearly saving: the years until the battery has paid for itself.</Recall>

</View>
